en: O Savior who knows all tastes, you who are obtainable through sweetness,
your name was never once taken by me;
forgive this offense, forgive this offense!
O Lord of compassionate heart, forgive my transgression. || 1 ||
O All-pervading Lord, due to the firmness of fate, your name was never once uttered by me while I was in another womb;
forgive this offense, forgive this offense!
Forgive this offense, O Lord, whose heart is moist with compassion.
Out of the suffering I endured while dwelling within my mother’s womb, I have never once called upon your name;
forgive this offense, forgive this offense.
Forgive this offense, O Lord of compassionate heart. || 3 ||
As soon as I was born, being utterly deluded, I never gave you a name.
Forgive this offense; forgive this offense.
Forgive this offense, O Lord of moistened heart. || 4 ||
While my mind was absorbed in play during my childhood, I never once gave you a name;
forgive this offense, forgive this offense!
Forgive this offense, O Lord of compassionate heart. || 5 ||
In my youth, out of ignorance and attachment to worldly enjoyments, I never once gave you your name;
forgive this offense, forgive this offense.
Forgive this offense, O Lord of compassionate heart.
By me, an old man whose senses are failing,
your name has never been uttered;
forgive this offense, forgive this offense.
Forgive this offense, O Lord of compassionate heart.
O Hṛṣīkeśa, O Hari, witness of the universe, forgive the offense born of my speech, mind, and body, whether committed knowingly or unknowingly;
forgive the offense, forgive the offense.
Forgive this offense, O Lord of compassionate heart.
Whether remembered, meditated upon, invoked, or worshipped;
whether sung, praised, or saluted; or even not recited—forgive this offense, forgive this offense!
Forgive this offense, O Lord, whose heart is moist with compassion.
O ocean of compassion, there is no one like you; may you become my refuge from this worldly existence, for you are my protector from the ocean of rebirth.
Just as the earth is the support for all things emerging from the ground, so are you my foundation.
Thus has the essence been requested and granted by the disciple. 10.
Thus ends the hymn for the expiation of offenses (*Aparādhakṣamāpana-stotra*) composed by the most venerable Śrīmad Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī Svāmī Mahārāja.
